title: Canonical Hosted Surface PRD & Launch Playbook for Generation, Chat, Embeddings, and Rerank
creator: Mina Lopez
description:
Overview: This PRD defines a canonical response surface and launch playbook for Redwood hosted endpoints across four primary capabilities: generation (completions), chat, embeddings, and rerank. The goal is to reduce integration friction for customers, make behavioral contracts explicit, and provide a repeatable checklist for safe launch.

Problem: Over the past two quarters we have accumulated variant behaviors across endpoint surfaces (schema differences, streaming vs non-streaming edge cases, inconsistent error semantics, and divergent default tokenization/normalization). These inconsistencies are a source of customer churn and increased support burden when customers integrate multiple endpoint types.

This document scopes the behavioral contract, required schema changes, rollout plan, and acceptance criteria for the canonical surface, and enumerates the launch checklist that PM/Eng/Design/Support must complete before GA.
goals: Define a single canonical response schema and error model for all hosted endpoints
Guarantee backward-compatible defaults where feasible, and document breaking changes with migration guidance
Provide testable acceptance criteria and telemetry thresholds for coverage and quality
Reduce support tickets related to cross-endpoint inconsistencies by 50% in the first 3 months post-GA
non_goals: Fundamental model architecture changes or new model onboarding (handled by Model Ops)
Major SDK redesigns; SDK teams will add compatibility shims where required
Complete deprecation of legacy endpoints in this release — deprecation plan will be separate
success_metrics: Integration success: 90% of internal integration tests pass in staging across all endpoints
Customer telemetry: < 15% increase in 30-day support requests related to endpoint semantics during rollout
Performance: median 95th percentile tail latency delta <= +10% vs baseline for each endpoint under standard traffic profile
Quality: embedding cosine-similarity regression < 0.02 on canonical test-suite for vector outputs
Adoption: 70% of new hosted API signups default to canonical surface within 2 months
scope: Generation (completions): canonical chunked streaming schema + final message envelope
Chat: canonical role/message structure, system messages preserved, tool-calling structured support
Embeddings: fixed dimensionality conventions, normalization flag, deterministic hashing for vectors
Rerank: plain scoring contract and top-k deterministic tie-break rules
Operational: telemetry naming conventions, per-route cost attribution, graceful fallback policies
requirements: REQ-1: Canonical Response Envelope - All endpoints return a top-level 'response' object containing 'id', 'model', 'timing', and 'output' fields. Acceptance: schema validated by JSON schema unit tests and example payloads stored in repo.
REQ-2: Streaming Contract - Streaming chunks MUST include 'chunk_id' and 'is_final' booleans. Acceptance: streaming client integration tests simulate mid-stream disconnect and resume behavior.

REQ-3: Error Semantics - Standardize HTTP error codes with machine-readable 'error.code' and human 'error.message'. Acceptance: error mapping documented and end-to-end tests assert mapping for 10 common failure modes.

REQ-4: Embeddings Determinism - Optional 'normalize=true' flag produces L2-normalized vectors; deterministic seed for tokenizer. Acceptance: regression harness compares 1000 sample inputs, asserting cosine variance within threshold.
REQ-5: Rerank Determinism - Rerank should include deterministic tie-break when scores equal; acceptance: unit tests with mocked scoring verify stable ordering across runs.

REQ-6: Backwards Compatibility Layer - Provide a compatibility query param '?compat=legacy' that restores legacy output shape for two quarters. Acceptance: compatibility flag returns pre-canonical schema in integration tests.
REQ-7: Telemetry & Cost Attribution - Each request must annotate model and route labels for cost attribution. Acceptance: console dashboard shows token-level cost breakdown for synthetic traffic run.
REQ-8: Documentation - Public API docs, SDK examples, migration guide, and a 'breaking-changes' changelog entry. Acceptance: docs PR merged and links included in launch checklist.
acceptance_criteria: All schema fields present and validated by CI (response.id, response.model, response.timing, response.output)
Streaming tests pass: 99% success on resume and finalization scenarios in staging
Performance regression within agreed budget across 3 load profiles (synth-low, synth-med, synth-high)
Security review completed and no critical findings (security_review_required=true)
Support playbook published with runbooks for common customer migration issues
Telemetry: 95th percentile of error-free requests instrumented with labels for per-route cost and latency
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): Deploy canonical surface to 5% of traffic for non-paying demo accounts and internal customers. Run smoke tests and telemetry validation for 72 hours.
Phase 1 (Limited): Expand to 25% including a subset of paying customers that opt-in; offer migration guidance and dedicated support channel.
Phase 2 (Ramp): 60% traffic with automated rollback monitoring for latency, error rates, and quality regressions; hold for 48 hours on anomalies.
Phase 3 (GA): Full rollout after sign-offs from Eng, Security, Support, and Docs. Announce deprecation timeline for legacy shapes (6 months from GA).
open_questions: Q1: Is the legacy compatibility layer sufficient for SDK consumers with low release velocity, or do we need a server-side adapter?
Q2: Should embedding normalization be opt-out instead of opt-in given downstream similarity expectations?
Q3: For rerank tie-break, do we prefer deterministic hash of document id or stable insertion order?
Q4: What telemetry retention window is required for cost dispute investigations (30 vs 90 days)?
decisions: D1: Adopt top-level 'response' envelope rather than deeply nested disparate keys to simplify parsing across languages.
D2: Streaming 'chunk_id' will be an incrementing integer to make client-side reassembly deterministic.
D3: Back-compat via '?compat=legacy' query param for 6 months; deprecation announced at GA with migration guide.
D4: Use deterministic hash of document id for rerank tie-break to avoid insertion-order flakiness.
updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Design, SDK, and Security. Agreed on envelope approach. Action: ENG to prototype streaming schema.
2026-03-02: ENG prototype complete for streaming and compatibility param. Initial perf regression +6% at 95th p90 on synth-med; Eng exploring micro-optimizations.
2026-03-05: Design review: clarified chat role preservation semantics and tool-calling JSON schema. Design requested clearer examples for nested function args.
2026-03-08: Docs PR opened. Security pre-review scheduled for 2026-03-12. Support to assemble migration FAQ by 2026-03-18.
2026-03-10: Decided deterministic rerank tie-break using document id hash (D4). Updated acceptance criteria to include rerank ordering tests.
checklist: 1) Engineering: Schema JSON schema committed + unit tests (PR merged)
2) Engineering: Streaming resume and finalization e2e tests in staging
3) Performance: Load test report for synth-low/med/high attached and within thresholds
4) Security: Security review completed and sign-off attached
5) Docs: Public docs, migration guide, and SDK examples published
6) Support: Playbook and dedicated ticket triage channel created
7) Design: API examples and message formatting guidelines published
8) Telemetry: Console dashboard shows per-route cost attribution and 72h smoke validation
9) Legal/Compliance: Export/KMS implications reviewed for embeddings (if applicable)
10) Launch comms: Customer-facing announcement and migration timeline prepared
